title: KV pool rebalancer and decode-latency orchestrator
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Under mixed workloads (short chat vs long context prefills) our paged KV cache can become imbalanced: hot shards consume most pool pages while many cold shards hold fragmented small pages. This causes spiky decode latency when long prefill requests need contiguous page space or when kernel selection forces cross-shard fetches.

Goal: Implement a background KV pool rebalancer that opportunistically compacts fragmented pages, migrates low-utilization entries to a smaller footprint, and proactively reserves decode-priority windows for imminent prefill work. The feature should reduce tail latency for prefill-heavy flows and smooth per-request variance without regressing throughput.

Scope: Design + implementation of a rebalancer controller, new page descriptor metadata (lightweight access counters + generation age), a prefill-latency hint API for the scheduler, and knobbed policies for live rollout. This ticket covers the runtime rebalancer and scheduler hooks; eviction heuristics tuning and KB/allocator micro-ops will be follow-ups if needed.
implementation_notes:
1) New page metadata: 16-bit generation, 32-bit recent_access_counter (decayed periodically), and a 1-byte frag_score (0-255) computed from hole count and free-run lengths. Store in page header to keep lookup O(1).

2) Rebalancer controller: periodic pass (configurable interval, default 30s) that scans shard summaries, picks candidate pages with frag_score>200 or generation>3 and low access counters, and issues move operations to assemble contiguous pages for long prefill requests. Moves should be batched and use background copy paths that respect memory pressure signals.

3) Migration strategy: prefer coalescing small fragments by migrating hot entries to new contiguous page blocks, then free small fragments into a global small-page free list. Avoid moving entries with recent decode affinity unless prefill_hint is set.

4) Prefill-latency orchestrator: scheduler API prefill_hint(request_id, expected_seq_len, deadline_ms). When invoked, the orchestrator will attempt to reserve N contiguous pages in the local shard (fallback to remote shard if impossible) and tag upcoming decode work with high decode_priority to steer kernel selection paths toward low-latency execution lanes.

5) Kernel routing integration: expose an execution preference flag (fast-path=true) to the kernel selector for decode jobs tagged by the orchestrator. Kernels supporting early-attention-streaming should be favored.

6) Safety: cap background move bandwidth (default 5% GPU memory BW) and stop rebalancer when tail SLOs worsen or GPU utilization > 85%. Rebalancer must be cancelable mid-batch and idempotent across restarts.
acceptance_criteria:
- End-to-end integration tests for rebalancer move+rollback behavior.
- Microbench: 95th percentile decode latency for mixed workload (50% chat short, 50% long prefill) reduces by at least 12% on our internal benchmark compared to baseline.
- No regression in throughput (>98% of baseline tokens/s).
- Feature flags and knobs available in runtime config and Redwood Console UI.
- Metrics: rebalancer_moves_total, rebalancer_move_failures, reserved_prefill_windows, prefill_miss_rate.
- Documentation: Confluence design doc + short runbook for disabling rebalancer if needed.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for page metadata encoding/decoding and frag_score calculation.
- Integration tests simulating fragmentation patterns and verifying that reserved windows succeed when space exists.
- Load test: 48-hour mixed-workload cluster run with rebalancer enabled and disabled; gather token throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, and memory pressure events.
- Fuzzing: random move aborts and crash-recovery scenarios to confirm idempotency.
- Canary rollout on dedicated: enable for 10% of shards for 24 hours, observe SLOs and rebalancer metrics then expand to 50%.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature behind runtime flag 'kv_rebalancer_v1' and scheduler flag 'prefill_orchestrator_v1'.
2) Internal canary: enable on non-critical dedicated cluster with low customer exposure. Monitor p95/p99 decode latency and rebalancer metrics for 48h.
3) Gradual ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 100% over 7 days if metrics stable.
4) Emergency rollback: flip flag off and drain in-flight moves. Run manual compaction tool if needed.
5) Post-rollout: keep reduced sampling of move traces (1%) for 30d for telemetry analysis.
monitoring:
Metrics: rebalancer.scan_duration_seconds, rebalancer.pages_examined, rebalancer.pages_moved, rebalancer.move_latency_seconds, prefill.window_reservations, prefill.reservation_failures, decode.priority_p90_latency.
Alerts: >1% reservation_failures over 5m, move_failures spike, rebalancer_bandwidth > configured threshold, decode_p99 increase >20% from baseline.
Dashboards: per-cluster and per-shard view showing fragmentation heatmap, reserved window counts, and kernel-selection mix (fast-path vs default).

notes:
Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive compaction improves p99 but increases background memory bandwidth and can interfere with caching heuristics. We picked conservative defaults and a prefill-hint to bias moves toward helpful windows.
- Could have used a global defragmenter sweep at low traffic times, but that approach risks long pauses; opted for incremental, cancelable moves.

Open questions:
- Whether to expose frag_score tuning to customers on Dedicated.
- How to coordinate rebalancer across shards when multi-shard prefill reservations are needed (future work).
